title: Microsoft extends its support lifecycle for business products to ten years, which pushes the end of Windows 2000 support to 2010
impact: Windows 2000 servers and clients can stay supported until 2010 instead of 2007, so replacing them can wait for the next hardware cycle

title: Microsoft extends its support lifecycle for developer products to ten years, which gives .NET Framework 1.0 extended support until 2009
impact: Apps on the 1.0 runtime can stay supported until 2009, but should be moved to a later framework before then

title: Microsoft extends its support lifecycle for developer products to ten years, which gives Visual Studio .NET 2002 extended support until 2009
impact: Teams still building with the 2002 IDE can stay supported until 2009, but should move to a newer IDE and framework before then

title: Microsoft announces an expanded support lifecycle policy with at least 10 years of support for business and developer products, under which Windows Server 2003 extended support runs to July 2015
impact: Servers bought for 2003 have a known end date, so server replacement and app moves to a newer Windows can be planned years ahead

title: Microsoft announces an expanded support lifecycle policy with at least 10 years of support for business and developer products, under which .NET Framework 1.1 support runs to October 2013
impact: Apps on the 1.1 runtime have a known end date, so a move to a later framework can be planned years ahead

title: Microsoft announces an expanded support lifecycle policy with at least 10 years of support for business and developer products, under which Visual Studio .NET 2003 extended support runs to October 2013
impact: Teams building with Visual Studio .NET 2003 have a known end date for the IDE, so the next IDE upgrade can be planned

title: Microsoft announces an expanded support lifecycle policy with at least 10 years of support for business and developer products, under which Office 2003 extended support runs to April 2014
impact: PCs moved to Office 2003 have a known end date, so the next Office upgrade and retesting of Excel and Access integrations can be planned

title: Windows XP Service Pack 2 is released to manufacturing with Windows Firewall on by default
impact: Client/server apps that listen on ports or use DCOM can stop working on updated PCs until firewall exceptions are set

title: Extended support for Windows NT 4.0 Server ends
impact: Servers still on NT 4.0 get no more security updates, pushing migration to Windows 2000 or Server 2003
